false_alarm_rate_heldout.source_note: held-out normal windows; NOT used for fitting, scaling, calibration or threshold choice
false_alarm_rate_heldout.heldout_source_warning: held-out rows come from the SAME simulation as train/calibration (chronological split): they block direct contamination, but the rows are autocorrelated across the split boundary, so this is not an independent process run

false_alarm_rate_heldout_non_overlapping.source_note: stride = window_size windows: far fewer, far less autocorrelated
false_alarm_rate_heldout_non_overlapping.n_windows_note: n_independent_windows is small; the CI upper bound, not the point estimate, is the defensible number

false_alarm_rate_note: false_alarm_rate_* are computed on HELD-OUT-NORMAL windows. Earlier revisions computed them on the calibration split — those (circular) numbers live under calibration_rate_*.
calibration_rate_note: computed on the SAME calibration windows that set q_alpha — circular by construction, NOT an estimate of false-alarm rate on unseen data. See false_alarm_rate_heldout for the held-out estimate.
never_flag_note: q_alpha is infinite: with calibration_stride=12 the calibration split yields only 5 effective windows; a finite (1-0.05) conformal quantile needs >= 19. Under split-conformal's never-flag rule the detector cannot emit UNCERTAIN/ABNORMAL, so FAR/delay metrics degrade to 'never flags' rather than a calibrated 5% error rate.

SafetySystems.flare_header_press (window.description: window mean of SafetySystems.flare_header_press over the 12-row window; threshold = train mean + k*std with k chosen so the calibration-window FAR <= alpha=0.05 (no peeking at held-out or fault-day data)
SafetySystems.flare_header_press (window.threshold_source: train-split windows only (no held-out, no fault-day rows)

SafetySystems.flare_header_press (mean p.description: mean per-tick slope of SafetySystems.flare_header_press over the 12-row window; threshold = train mean + k*std with k chosen so the calibration-window FAR <= alpha=0.05 (no peeking at held-out or fault-day data)
SafetySystems.flare_header_press (mean p.threshold_source: train-split windows only (no held-out, no fault-day rows)

detector_vs_baselines.summary: The conformal autoencoder produced NO detection. The fastest baseline (SafetySystems.flare_header_press (window mean)) detected in 0.0 h, so the baseline is strictly better on this scenario.

provenance.seed_note: dataset.random_seed; seeds random, numpy and torch
